summary: This Dockerfile builds a container for a FastAPI web application. It starts with Python 3.11, installs FastAPI and its dependencies, copies your application code in, and configures the container to run the app on port 80 when started.

explanations.2: python:3.11-slim is a pre-built image with Python 3.11 already installed; the 'slim' version is smaller because it excludes unnecessary packages.
explanations.5: WORKDIR sets /code as the default directory inside the container, so future commands run from there.
explanations.9: The --no-cache-dir flag tells pip not to save downloaded packages locally, which saves space in the final image; 'fastapi[all]' installs FastAPI plus optional extras like uvicorn.
explanations.12: COPY takes the main.py file from your computer and places it into the /code directory inside the container.
explanations.15: EXPOSE tells Docker (and whoever uses this image) that the app listens on port 80, though it doesn't actually open the port—you do that when running the container.
explanations.18: CMD sets the default command to run when the container starts; it launches uvicorn (the web server) pointing to the 'app' object in main.py, listening on all network interfaces (0.0.0.0) at port 80.
